newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan jobless rate falls, but worries remain -- govt.
newsitem.headline: Japan jobless rate falls, but worries remain -- govt.

text.p: Japan's jobless rate edged down in August, continuing a steady drop from record high levels, but the worst is not over yet, with some jobs data showing discouraging signs, official figures showed on Tuesday.

"Unemployment has dropped for the second month in a row. But there are still worrying factors such as an increase in middle-aged and older unemployed people," an official at the government's Management and Coordination Agency told reporters.
The unemployment rate fell to 3.3 percent in August after dropping to 3.4 percent in July from a record high of 3.5 percent in the preceding two months.

Although Japan does not have the double-digit jobless rates of some Western countries, a climb in the rate over the past year has rattled a nation which has had minimal unemployment for most of the postwar era.

The jobless rate among workers over 55 years of age rose by 0.9 percentage point to 4.2 percent in August due to continuous efforts by Japanese companies to streamline their operations amid a prolonged business slump.
"We cannot say definitely that there has been a change in the basic jobless trend," the official said.
Job openings, which had risen for the third month in a row in July, fell to 71 openings for every 100 job seekers in August from 72 openings in July.
"The drop in the job openings may be a sign of a sluggish economic recovery," Satoshi Shimamoto, a senior economist at MMS International, told Reuters Financial Television.
He said there will be increased pressure on Japanese companies to reduce their number of mature workers as it is costly to keep the highly paid portion of their workforce.
